diagnosis.rootCause: At 19:00:01Z the container image was changed from `ghcr.io/joshthemenace/dex-api:latest` to `dex-api:dev`. A name with no registry defaults to Docker Hub, where `library/dex-api` doesn't exist, so the new pod can't pull it. The old pods can't fall back either, because ghcr returns 403 to anonymous pulls and the Deployment has no `imagePullSecrets`.
diagnosis.summary: dex-api has no running pods: neither its new image dex-api:dev nor the old ghcr image can be pulled.
unresolved: Whether dex-api:dev is meant to be a locally built image loaded into a kind node: confirm with `kind get clusters` and `docker exec dex-control-plane crictl images | grep dex-api`.

steps.text: Check whether this is a kind cluster with the image loaded. Run `kind get clusters` and `docker exec dex-control-plane crictl images | grep dex`. If `dex-api:dev` is missing from the node, the next step applies.

Load the local images into the kind node. Run `kind load docker-image dex-api:dev dex-web:dev --name dex`, then `kubectl -n dex rollout restart deploy/dex-api deploy/dex-web`. Also set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` explicitly so the node never tries Docker Hub.
steps.precondition: Cluster is kind and dex-api:dev was built locally

steps.text: Otherwise, use the ghcr image with a pull secret. Run `kubectl -n dex create secret docker-registry ghcr --docker-server=ghcr.io --docker-username=joshthemenace --docker-password=<PAT with read:packages>`. Add `imagePullSecrets: [{name: ghcr}]` to the pod spec and set the image back to `ghcr.io/joshthemenace/dex-api:latest`.
steps.precondition: The intended image lives in the private ghcr repo

diagnosis.report:
I found the cause: both images dex-api uses fail to download, so its app has never started. Think of it as asking for a package by a nickname that only your local post office knows. The other office can't find it, and the backup address (ghcr) refuses to deliver without a key.

[[radar:evidence=0]]

At 19:00:01Z, in the same second the Deployment was created, its image changed from `ghcr.io/joshthemenace/dex-api:latest` to `dex-api:dev`. An image name with no registry in front means Docker Hub (`docker.io/library/dex-api:dev`), and that repository doesn't exist. The two pods left over from the first version can't take over either: ghcr returns **403 Forbidden** to an anonymous pull, and the pod spec has no `imagePullSecrets` (the stored login Kubernetes uses to pull from a private registry).

[[radar:evidence=1|compact]]

No container has started, so this isn't an app bug. The logs only say the container is waiting on the image pull. The sibling Deployment dex-web fails the same way (`dex-web:dev` plus ghcr `:latest`), so the same fix applies to both.

[[radar:evidence=2|compact]]

**What I couldn't confirm:** a `:dev` image with no registry usually means an image built on your machine for a local cluster. The node name `dex-control-plane` suggests a kind cluster (Kubernetes running inside Docker), and in kind a locally built image has to be copied onto the node before pods can use it. That's an inference from the name, so I didn't recommend a single fix. Run the verify step first. If the image isn't on the node, load it with `kind load` (step 2). If the real image is the private ghcr one, add a pull secret instead (step 3).

The audit findings (privilege escalation, auto-mounted service account token) are hardening issues and have nothing to do with this outage.
diagnosis.notes:
**Evidence ledger**
- `diagnose` dex/dex-api (ev_…cxjir76e33…): the image was changed from `ghcr.io/joshthemenace/dex-api:latest` to `dex-api:dev` at 19:00:01Z, in the same second the Deployment was created. Pulling `dex-api:dev` fails on Docker Hub (`docker.io/library/dex-api:dev`, repository not found or access denied). Pulling the ghcr image fails with a 403 on the anonymous token request. The pod template has no `imagePullSecrets`. It does not show which images are cached on the node or the template's `imagePullPolicy`.
- `list_resources` pods in dex (ev_…lpz5fdunisa…): one dex-api pod is on `dex-api:dev` and two old-revision pods are on the ghcr `:latest` image, all in ImagePullBackOff on node `dex-control-plane`. The sibling Deployment dex-web shows the same pattern. Point-in-time, dex namespace only.
- Alternative: the app crashes on start. Ruled out because no container has started yet (every log read reports "waiting to start: trying and failing to pull image").
- Alternative: the cluster is kind and the local image was never loaded into the node. This is inferred from the node name and is untested.

remediation: Check whether this is a kind cluster with the image loaded. Run `kind get clusters` and `docker exec dex-control-plane crictl images | grep dex`. If `dex-api:dev` is missing from the node, the next step applies.

Load the local images into the kind node. Run `kind load docker-image dex-api:dev dex-web:dev --name dex`, then `kubectl -n dex rollout restart deploy/dex-api deploy/dex-web`. Also set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` explicitly so the node never tries Docker Hub.

Otherwise, use the ghcr image with a pull secret. Run `kubectl -n dex create secret docker-registry ghcr --docker-server=ghcr.io --docker-username=joshthemenace --docker-password=<PAT with read:packages>`. Add `imagePullSecrets: [{name: ghcr}]` to the pod spec and set the image back to `ghcr.io/joshthemenace/dex-api:latest`.
